result.answer_markdown:
## Taiwanese beef noodle soup

Here’s a cozy take on Taiwanese beef noodle soup using the ingredients available to you. The omitted seasonings mean the broth will be simpler, but the beef, aromatics, and warm spices still bring plenty of character.

### Ingredients (for 2 servings, at Walmart)

- Beef shank: about 400 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- Wheat noodles: about 200 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- Soy sauce: about 40 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- Ginger: about 20 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- Garlic: about 12 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- Scallions: about 24 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- Onion: about 60 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- Tomato: about 80 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- Cinnamon: about 0.6 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- Great Value Ground Black Pepper 3 oz: about 0.4 g (substitute for Sichuan peppercorns, from Walmart)
- Bay leaf: about 0.2 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- Rock sugar: about 6 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- Bok choy: about 120 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- Vegetable oil: about 10 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- ~~Doubanjiang~~: left out, no suitable substitute
- ~~Shaoxing wine~~: left out, no suitable substitute
- ~~Star anise~~: left out, no suitable substitute
- ~~Pickled mustard greens~~: left out, no suitable substitute

### Substitutions

| Original | Use instead | Price | Taste / texture | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Doubanjiang | no substitute found (skip it) | | Leaving it out will make the broth less savory, fermented, and chili-forward. | No suitable chili-bean-sauce stand-in was found in the Walmart catalog. |
| Shaoxing wine | no substitute found (skip it) | | Without it, the broth will lose a little of its mellow, aromatic depth. | No suitable cooking-wine product was found in the Walmart catalog. |
| Star anise | no substitute found (skip it) | | Omitting it reduces the broth's sweet, licorice-like aroma. | No suitable cinnamon stand-in was found in the Walmart catalog. |
| Sichuan peppercorns | Great Value Ground Black Pepper 3 oz | $1.98 (unverified) | Adds ordinary peppery heat, but lacks Sichuan peppercorns' citrusy aroma and numbing tingle. | Ground black pepper is available and can add some warmth, though it is only a partial flavor match. |
| Pickled mustard greens | no substitute found (skip it) | | Leaving them out removes a crisp, tangy, salty contrast from the soup. | No suitable pickled greens option was found in the Walmart catalog. |

### Nutrition data used (USDA food for each ingredient)

- Beef shank: Beef, chuck for stew, separable lean and fat, choice, raw
- Wheat noodles: Noodles, egg, dry, enriched
- Soy sauce: Soy sauce made from soy (tamari)
- Ginger: Ginger root, raw
- Garlic: Garlic, raw
- Scallions: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb), raw
- Onion: Onions, raw
- Tomato: Tomatoes, red, ripe, raw, year round average
- Cinnamon: Spices, cinnamon, ground
- Great Value Ground Black Pepper 3 oz: Spices, pepper, black
- Bay leaf: Spices, bay leaf
- Rock sugar: Sugars, brown
- Bok choy: Cabbage, chinese (pak-choi), raw
- Vegetable oil: Oil, vegetable, soybean, refined

### Steps

1. Cut the beef shank into chunks. Slice the ginger, garlic, scallions, onion, and tomato; trim the bok choy.
2. Warm the vegetable oil in a heavy pot. Add the beef and brown it, turning the pieces as they cook.
3. Add the ginger, garlic, scallions, onion, tomato, cinnamon, black pepper, bay leaf, rock sugar, and soy sauce. Stir, cover, and cook gently until the beef is tender, about 2–3 hours. Check occasionally and stir so the ingredients do not stick.
4. Cook the wheat noodles according to their package directions. Add the bok choy to the beef pot near the end and cook until tender. Remove the bay leaf.
5. Divide the noodles between bowls and spoon the beef, bok choy, and pot juices over them.

### What will taste different

Without doubanjiang, Shaoxing wine, star anise, and pickled mustard greens, the soup will be less chili-forward, fermented, and aromatic, with less tangy contrast. Black pepper brings ordinary peppery heat instead of Sichuan peppercorns’ citrusy aroma and numbing tingle.
